A US 9:00 start is 18:30 IST (ET summer), 19:30 (ET winter), 21:30 (PT summer) or 22:30 (PT winter); re-computed with IANA tzdata. Remote-first companies mitigate this with async norms (GitLab), but managers still ask what overlap a candidate offers (heuristic).

hiring_routes.route: H-1B, cap-subject (private US employer, consular processing from India)
hiring_routes.fits_when: A US company wants him on site in the US, is willing to sponsor and can wait for the next lottery cycle. The route is strongest when the offer is at a higher OEWS wage level for the role and location, because that earns more lottery entries.
hiring_routes.key_requirements: A specialty-occupation job and a qualifying degree (he holds a B.E. and an M.Eng in AI & ML; counsel should confirm eligibility). The employer registers ($215) and, if selected, files an LCA and an I-129. Weighted selection gives Level IV 4 entries, III 3, II 2 and I 1. His master's is non-US, so the 20,000 US advanced-degree allocation does not apply. Employer-paid fees: I-129 $780 ($460 small employer/nonprofit), Asylum Program Fee $600/$300/$0, ACWIA $750 (1-25 FTE) or $1,500 (26+), fraud fee $500, and optional premium processing at $2,965. The $100,000 payment (Proclamation 10973) applies to beneficiaries abroad; reports that courts have blocked it and that it was extended in Sep 2026 are UNVERIFIED here. A reported $103,265 cap-subject fee proposal and the proposed DOL wage-level increases are not in effect. General information, not legal advice.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: Registration fee: since the FY2026 season (2024 fee rule). Weighted rule: effective 27 Feb 2026. Filing fees: USCIS schedule in force since 1 Apr 2024. Premium processing $2,965 since 1 Mar 2026. These were checked against reviewer knowledge to mid-2026, not re-fetched. The $100k litigation (Jun-Oct 2026), the $103,265 NPRM (Aug 2026) and the DOL NPRM (Mar 2026) are reported and unverified as of 18 Oct 2026.
hiring_routes.processing_time: Annual cycle. FY2027 registration ran in March 2026, and that season is over. The next opportunity is the FY2028 registration (expected around March 2027 based on prior years; not yet announced), with a start no earlier than 1 Oct 2027. Premium processing gives an action within 15 business days. Consular stamping in India follows; appointments there were rescheduled months out after the Dec 2025 online-presence review.

hiring_routes.route: H-1B, cap-exempt (US universities, their related or affiliated nonprofits, and nonprofit or governmental research organizations)
hiring_routes.fits_when: Research-engineer or research roles at universities or qualifying research institutes. This aligns with his evaluation research and the PhD applications his preprint is aimed at.
hiring_routes.key_requirements: The same H-1B petition basics, but no lottery and no numerical cap. Since the H-1B modernization final rule (effective 17 Jan 2025), an organization for which basic or applied research is a 'fundamental activity' can qualify as a nonprofit or governmental research organization; it no longer has to be 'primarily engaged' in research. Per USCIS guidance of 20 Oct 2025, the $100,000 payment applies to cap-exempt employers for beneficiaries outside the US whenever it is enforceable. The reported $103,265 proposal would reportedly not apply to cap-exempt petitions (unverified). General information, not legal advice.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: Cap-exemption definitions per 8 CFR 214.2(h)(19) as amended effective 17 Jan 2025. $100k applicability per USCIS guidance of 20 Oct 2025; current enforcement status unverified as of 18 Oct 2026.
hiring_routes.processing_time: Can be filed year-round. Premium processing gives an action within 15 business days ($2,965); consular processing in India follows.

hiring_routes.route: O-1A (extraordinary ability in sciences, education, business or athletics)
hiring_routes.fits_when: A longer-term route once a public record of distinction exists. There is no lottery and no cap, and the employer or an agent petitions. None of the usual evidence (awards, peer-reviewed publications, press coverage, judging roles) is listed in the verified profile facts, and his research is not yet peer-reviewed. This is therefore an evidence-building track rather than a near-term option (assessment, not legal advice).
hiring_routes.key_requirements: 'Sustained national or international acclaim': either a major internationally recognized award, or at least 3 of 8 regulatory criteria, followed by a final-merits review of the whole record. The criteria are: awards, selective memberships, published material about the person, judging others' work, original contributions of major significance, scholarly authorship, a critical role at distinguished organizations, and high remuneration. A peer advisory opinion (consultation) is usually required. The Jan 2025 Policy Manual update clarified, among other things, that a company owned by the beneficiary can be the petitioner. Fees: I-129 $1,055 ($530 small employer/nonprofit) plus the Asylum Program Fee of $600/$300/$0; optional premium processing $2,965. Initial stay of up to 3 years.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: Criteria per the USCIS O-1 page and Policy Manual Vol. 2 Part M (Jan 2025 update). Fees per the 2024 fee rule. Premium fee since 1 Mar 2026. Reviewer knowledge to mid-2026; not re-fetched.
hiring_routes.processing_time: Regular processing times vary: check the USCIS processing-times page. Secondary estimates conflict and could not be verified, so no figure is given. Premium processing gives an action within 15 business days; an RFE stops the clock, and a new 15-business-day period starts on response. Consular processing in India adds time, and appointment availability there has been volatile.

hiring_routes.route: L-1 intracompany transfer (general concept only)
hiring_routes.fits_when: Someone employed abroad by a multinational with a qualifying US parent, branch, subsidiary or affiliate. This is stated only as a concept: nothing here implies any transfer offer or eligibility at his current employer.
hiring_routes.key_requirements: At least one continuous year of employment abroad with the qualifying organization within the three years before the petition. L-1A is for executive or managerial roles; L-1B (not researched in detail here) is for specialized knowledge. L-1A allows an initial stay of up to 3 years (1 year for a new office), with extensions in increments of up to 2 years to a 7-year maximum. Large employers may use a blanket L petition. Not subject to the H-1B lottery.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: USCIS L-1A page and Policy Manual Vol. 2 Part L; one-year counting per the 2018 USCIS policy memo as summarized by BAL. Reviewer knowledge to mid-2026; not re-fetched.
hiring_routes.processing_time: No annual cycle. Premium processing is available ($2,965, 15 business days). Consular stamping in India follows.

hiring_routes.route: Remote employment from India via an Employer of Record (or via the US company's own Indian entity)
hiring_routes.fits_when: A US team wants him full-time and long-term without visa timelines, and can work async with partial overlap. This is the fastest path to a full-time role on a US team from Bengaluru.
hiring_routes.key_requirements: An Indian legal employer (an EOR or a subsidiary) issues an Indian employment contract and handles PF, ESI, gratuity and TDS, while the US company directs the work. The four Labour Codes have been in force since 21 Nov 2025; check the status of their implementing rules (not verified here). An EOR does not by itself remove permanent-establishment risk; engineering roles without contract-signing authority are generally lower risk (vendor guidance). Vendor list prices and statutory-cost estimates were not verified, so get quotes. General information, not legal or tax advice.

hiring_routes.processing_time: Set by the notice period (unknown; needs confirmation) and the employer's offer process. Vendor claims of onboarding within days are unverified marketing.

hiring_routes.route: Independent contractor from India (direct B2B or through a contractor platform)
hiring_routes.fits_when: Genuinely project-scoped work: a defined deliverable, his own tools and schedule, and no exclusivity. Suitable for a trial engagement or an evaluation or RAG audit, not for a disguised full-time role.

Pay for services performed entirely outside the US is generally foreign-source income; confirm with the IRS instructions and a tax adviser. Indian reclassification risk exists if the arrangement looks like employment (control, integration, exclusivity; vendor sources). Any confidentiality obligations to his current employer must be checked before taking on side work. General information, not legal or tax advice.

corrected.timezone: Bengaluru uses IST (UTC+05:30) with no daylight saving time. US offsets: EDT UTC-4 and PDT UTC-7 until 1 Nov 2026; EST UTC-5 and PST UTC-8 from 1 Nov 2026 to 14 Mar 2027; DST again until 7 Nov 2027. All of this was re-computed on 18 Oct 2026 from IANA tzdata via Python zoneinfo, and every figure here matched. IST is therefore 9.5 h ahead of ET and 12.5 h ahead of PT in US summer, and 10.5 h and 13.5 h ahead in US winter. A US 9:00-17:00 workday in IST: ET summer 18:30-02:30; ET winter 19:30-03:30; PT summer 21:30-05:30; PT winter 22:30-06:30. Example IST windows and their overlap with US 9-17: (a) 14:00-23:00 IST gives 4.5 h ET and 1.5 h PT in summer, 3.5 h and 0.5 h in winter; (b) 16:00-01:00 IST gives 6.5 h ET and 3.5 h PT in summer, 5.5 h and 2.5 h in winter; (c) a 4-hour evening block of 18:30-22:30 IST gives 4 h ET and 1 h PT in summer, 3 h and 0 h in winter. Practical reading (heuristic): East Coast teams can get 3-4 h of live overlap from an IST evening, while West Coast teams need a late IST evening or an async handoff model. GitLab's handbook (primary source) recommends async by default, recorded meetings, and deadlines with an explicit time zone instead of 'EOD'. Vendor blogs suggest a floor of 2-4 h of daily overlap (vendor heuristic, not verified). On the site, show one concrete window in IST plus ET/PT with a note that it shifts by 1 h when US clocks change. The hours themselves are UNKNOWN until Swaroop confirms what he will offer. Sources: https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zones/ist, https://www.iana.org/time-zones, https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/communication/, https://www.wisemonk.io/blogs/timezone-overlap-strategies-india-us-teams
corrected.resume_norms: US conventions, from university career offices: leave photo, date of birth, marital status and visa or citizenship details off the resume (Pomona: https://cdo.pomona.edu/resources/u-s-resume-tips-for-international-students/ ; CSU East Bay flyer: https://www.csueastbay.edu/careercenter/files/docs/career-services/guidestogo-international-student-career-flyer.pdf). Work authorization is captured by the application form's two screening questions, which DOJ treats as appropriate (https://www.justice.gov/media/1248166/dl). Length: one page is the dominant advice for early-career candidates, and 1-2 pages is acceptable (Pomona), so offer the one-page PDF first and the detailed PDF second. Layout: single column with clear section headers. In Ladders' 2018 eye-tracking study (7.4 s average initial screen), simple layouts with headers performed best and multi-column or cluttered layouts worst (https://www.hrdive.com/news/recruiters-spend-74-seconds-looking-at-your-resume/541582/). Bullets: Bock's 'Accomplished X as measured by Y by doing Z' with a baseline (https://www.businessinsider.in/googles-former-hr-boss-says-this-is-the-key-to-a-perfect-resume/articleshow/54925993.cms); Harvard: specific, active, fact-based, 'quantify and qualify' (https://careerservices.fas.harvard.edu/resources/hes-create-impactful-resumes-and-cover-letters/). Recruiters, sourcers and panels read differently, so tailor per role (Orosz: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/how-to-write-a-developer-resume-recruiters-will-read/). Never use hidden text or prompt injection; Greenhouse (Nov 2025) is cited as reporting that 22% of US hiring managers had found it (figure not re-verified). Applied to Swaroop (heuristics): a header of 'Bengaluru, India · email · LinkedIn · GitHub · site', with no phone on any publicly hosted PDF (PROFILE rule: never publish the phone). Lead with 'Associate Machine Learning Engineer, AI Platform & Agent Systems, ResMed (US-headquartered medical-device company)'. Show 'CGPA 9.08' (add the scale once Swaroop confirms it) and spell out Manipal School of Information Sciences, MAHE. Use the verified metrics with baselines, plus one line: 'Research (in progress, not peer-reviewed): pre-registered 9,253-query study…'. Group skills as LLM/agents · retrieval · platform/infra · classical ML. No salary.

hiring_routes.route: Germany: EU Blue Card (Section 18g of the Residence Act)
hiring_routes.fits_when: A job offer in Germany at or above EUR 50,700 gross a year, which needs no Federal Employment Agency (BA) approval. Or at or above EUR 45,934.20 for shortage occupations, including ICT professionals, or for someone whose degree is less than 3 years old; that tier needs BA approval. Swaroop's M.Eng. is from 2026, so the recent-graduate tier may apply, but the employer or counsel must confirm.
hiring_routes.key_requirements: A recognised degree: an anabin printout, or a ZAB statement of comparability if the university isn't listed. A concrete job offer. Guaranteed fixed gross pay; bonuses don't count. For the reduced tier, BA approval of pay and terms. Optionally, the employer-run fast-track procedure (section 81a).
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: 2026 calendar-year thresholds: 50% and 45.3% of the 2026 statutory pension contribution ceiling (EUR 101,400), adjusted every 1 January. A Federal Foreign Office FAQ was reported to show EUR 50,760 (not verified); use the BA / Make it in Germany figure.
hiring_routes.processing_time: Fast track: the mission should give an appointment within 3 weeks and usually decides within 3 weeks of a complete application. Fees: EUR 411 for the fast-track procedure, EUR 75 for the national visa. Not re-verified: about 4 months overall including recognition and approval; a roughly 3-week decision for regular Blue Card visas; faster appointments through the Consular Services Portal in India.

hiring_routes.route: Germany: Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte), a job-search permit he would apply for himself
hiring_routes.fits_when: He wants to search for work in Germany before an employer has to act, and is willing to fund his stay
hiring_routes.key_requirements: Either a qualification fully recognised in Germany (no points needed), or a university degree or at least 2-year vocational qualification state-recognised in the issuing country, plus German at A1 or English at B2, and at least 6 points. Proof of funds through a blocked account or a declaration of commitment: re-check the current monthly amount (EUR 1,027 in 2024 and EUR 1,091 in 2025 to the checker's knowledge; the 2026 figure may differ). Health insurance. Valid up to 1 year. Allows part-time work up to 20 hours a week and trial work of up to 2 weeks.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: Rules as introduced in June 2024. The funds amount is updated each year; the 2026 value was not verified.
hiring_routes.processing_time: No official standard figure found. National visa appointment queues in India apply.

hiring_routes.route: Netherlands: Highly Skilled Migrant (kennismigrant) scheme
hiring_routes.fits_when: The employer is an IND-recognised sponsor and pays a market-rate gross monthly salary, excluding holiday allowance, of at least EUR 5,942 (age 30+) or EUR 4,357 (under 30). The reduced EUR 3,122 criterion is for graduates who meet the orientation-year conditions and apply within 3 years of graduating.
hiring_routes.key_requirements: Only the recognised sponsor can apply. Market-rate salary. An employment contract. A self-declaration of no criminal record. The sponsor has record-keeping, information and duty-of-care obligations. Pending (not verified): a July 2025 government proposal to tighten the scheme, including higher salary criteria; check its status. Tax: the 30% ruling is legislated to fall to 27% from 1 Jan 2027; reports of a planned partial reversal were not verified.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: 2026 amounts, valid 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2026. Consistent with about 4.46% indexation of the 2025 amounts; re-check on ind.nl before quoting.
hiring_routes.processing_time: The IND aims to decide in 2 weeks for complete applications from recognised sponsors; the legal maximum is 90 days. Not verified: a power, reported from 22 May 2026, to extend first applications by 30 days.

hiring_routes.route: Netherlands: EU Blue Card
hiring_routes.fits_when: A higher-education degree holder with a Dutch offer of at least EUR 5,942 a month, or EUR 4,754 a month under the reduced (recent-graduate) criterion
hiring_routes.key_requirements: A higher-education qualification. Salary at or above the threshold. Holiday allowance and pay in kind don't count; fixed allowances such as a guaranteed 13th month do.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: 2026 amounts (IND), consistent with indexation of the 2025 amounts; re-check before quoting
hiring_routes.processing_time: Same IND decision-period framework as above

hiring_routes.route: United Kingdom: Skilled Worker visa
hiring_routes.fits_when: A UK employer with a sponsor licence offers a role at RQF level 6 or above, paying the higher of GBP 41,700 and the occupation's going rate in the current Appendix Skilled Occupations. Look up the going rate for the SOC code the employer uses; the earlier GBP 54,700 figure for SOC 2134 was not verified. New entrants qualify at GBP 33,400 and 70% of the going rate. 'New entrant' covers, for example, people under 26 on the application date and people switching from Student or Graduate visas. His age is unknown, so don't assume.
hiring_routes.key_requirements: A sponsor licence and a Certificate of Sponsorship. The employer pays the Immigration Skills Charge: GBP 1,320 for the first 12 months (medium or large sponsor) or GBP 480 (small), for certificates assigned from 16 Dec 2025. English at CEFR B2 for applications from 8 Jan 2026. The applicant pays the visa fee (GBP 769 up to 3 years and GBP 1,519 over 3 years from outside the UK under the April 2025 schedule; a later increase to GBP 819 / GBP 1,618 was reported but not verified) and the Immigration Health Surcharge of GBP 1,035 a year.
hiring_routes.figures_as_of: GBP 41,700 threshold from 22 Jul 2025; Immigration Skills Charge from 16 Dec 2025; B2 English from 8 Jan 2026. Going rates and visa fees must be checked on gov.uk at the time of quoting.
hiring_routes.processing_time: About 3 weeks from outside the UK. Priority service gives a decision within 5 working days. Whether super-priority (next working day) is currently offered in India was not verified.

hiring_routes.processing_time: Not established; check gov.uk

hiring_routes.route: Ireland: Critical Skills Employment Permit
hiring_routes.fits_when: An offer for an occupation on the Critical Skills Occupations List with a relevant degree, at or above the current minimum. corrected.timezone: IST is UTC+5:30 all year; India has no daylight saving time. Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden use CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer. The UK uses GMT (UTC+0) and BST (UTC+1), and so does Ireland (UTC+0 / UTC+1). In 2026 Europe returns to winter time on Sunday 25 Oct at 01:00 UTC. So IST is 3:30 ahead of CEST, 4:30 ahead of CET and BST, and 5:30 ahead of GMT. The overlap figures below are arithmetic from those offsets. A European 10:00–16:00 core block falls at 13:30–19:30 IST in summer and 14:30–20:30 IST in winter for CET hubs. For London and Dublin it falls at 14:30–20:30 IST in summer and 15:30–21:30 IST in winter. A shifted IST day of 12:30–21:30 would cover that core block in full, all year, for every hub listed. Swaroop has not confirmed what overlap he will offer, so the site should show '[overlap hours: TO CONFIRM]'. Sources: https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zones/ist, https://www.timeanddate.com/news/time/europe-dst-end-2026.html, https://www.timeanddate.com/time/change/uk/london?year=2026
corrected.resume_norms:
These are 2025–2026 norms; sources are listed under the 'country-appropriate CV' priority. They were not re-opened in the fact-check, but they are low-risk, attributed advice.

- **UK:** No photo. Leave out personal details such as age, date of birth, marital status and nationality (National Careers Service). Prospects says no photo unless the job is acting or modelling.
- **Ireland:** 1–2 A4 pages (JobsIreland); GradIreland suggests aiming for one and two at most, and says date of birth, marital status and gender aren't needed. No official Irish source on photos was found; practitioner sources lean towards leaving it off.
- **Germany:** A tabular, reverse-chronological CV of one to two A4 pages (Bundesagentur für Arbeit). A photo is optional but many employers still expect one. Marital status and religion are not required.
- **Netherlands:** 1–2 pages; two is fine for experienced candidates (Leiden International Centre, practitioner source). Lead with achievements and numbers. A photo is optional, and practice varies. A short motivation letter carries weight.
- **Sweden:** About two pages at most, sent as a PDF, photo optional. Cover letter one page. Write in Swedish unless the posting says otherwise (Arbetsförmedlingen).
- **EU-wide:** Europass guidance suggests including a photo only if it is required.
- **Tech-specific:** Impact first, technologies at the end of each entry, no self-ratings (The Tech Resume Inside Out).

**Recommendation:** Publish one 'EU/UK' CV of at most 2 pages, with no photo and no personal data beyond name, email, LinkedIn, GitHub and city. Keep the portrait on the About page and for OG sharing, but out of the CV. Never include the phone number.

corrected.notes:
**How this fact-check was done, and its limits:**
- No live re-verification was possible on 18 Oct 2026. The WebSearch budget for the turn was already used up, WebFetch could not resolve any host, and the egress proxy refused a direct HTTPS request to www.gov.uk.
- 'Confirmed' therefore means one of three things: consistent with the checker's knowledge to about mid-2026; supported by arithmetic (for example, the German Blue Card thresholds are 50% and 45.3% of the 2026 pension contribution ceiling of EUR 101,400, and the Dutch 2026 amounts are a uniform roughly 4.46% indexation of the 2025 amounts); or checked against local files (the site copy, the codebase audit, PROFILE_FACTS.md).
- Anything dated after about June 2026, or that the checker could not recall reliably, is marked 'not verified' in the findings. That covers the Swedish June 2026 rules, the Digital Omnibus as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Irish 2026 thresholds and processing dates, the UK going rate for SOC 2134 and 2026 visa fees, company postings and 2026 surveys. Re-check every number on the live official page before publishing.

**Corrections made:**
- Remote access from India by an EU employer's own employee is not automatically a GDPR transfer (EDPB Guidelines 05/2021); contractor or employer-of-record set-ups generally are.
- The April 2025 LLM privacy report is a Support Pool of Experts report, not EDPB guidance.
- The first-interaction AI disclosure duty comes from AI Act Art. 50(1) and 50(5) themselves.
- The Opportunity Card points route also needs a state-recognised qualification and German A1 or English B2.
- The Global Talent wording that contradicted itself on Tech Nation is fixed.
- The 12:30–21:30 IST window fully covers a 10:00–16:00 core block, not 'almost all' of it.
- The Eurostat Blue Card shares are removed (unverifiable).

**Statements about Swaroop not in PROFILE_FACTS.md were stripped or reworded:** 'least-privilege', 'customer data stays in the customer's own bucket', 'human approval before answers go live', and 'a platform used to create' (now 'a platform he contributed to').

**Open conflicts:**
- Germany: EUR 50,760 in one Federal Foreign Office FAQ against EUR 50,700; the arithmetic supports EUR 50,700.
- UK: whether visa fees are GBP 769/1,519 (April 2025) or a later GBP 819/1,618.
- Netherlands: the 30% ruling falls to 27% from 2027 as legislated; a reported partial reversal and the July 2025 threshold proposal are unverified.
- Ireland: the Trusted Partner queue status.
- Sweden: the Blue Card threshold reported as unchanged.
- Robert Half 67% is US data; the Booking.com postings were read through aggregators.

**Disclaimers and handling:**
- Immigration and regulatory content is general information, not legal advice. Any page on Swaroop's site that mentions routes should say so and link to the official sources, without quoting thresholds unless they are re-checked.
- Eligibility hints that depend on unknowns (UK new-entrant status, Dutch under-30 or reduced criterion, Irish recent-graduate threshold, German recent-graduate tier) are for Swaroop and the employer to confirm. Do not publish them.
- **Codebase:** a 'For European teams' route fits the existing `<template data-route>` pattern. Static per-case pages would fix shareability and indexing. The site uses .nojekyll and serves from main, so any .md committed there is public; keep strategy notes out of main.

hesitations.hesitation: Work-pass process adds time and steps before an offer can be made
hesitations.why: For an Employment Pass, the employer (not the candidate) must first advertise on MyCareersFuture for at least 14 consecutive days unless exempt. Exemptions: fixed monthly salary of S$22,500 or more (since 1 Sep 2023), firms with fewer than 10 employees, intra-corporate transferees, and roles of 1 month or less. MOM then processes most online applications within 10 business days, and some take longer. Flagged, not re-verified on 18 Oct 2026: whether editing the ad restarts the 14-day count, MOM's guidance on when an offer may be made, and the in-principle approval validity period (previously reported as 6 months). Check these on MOM. Do not imply a ResMed transfer. General information, not legal advice.

hesitations.hesitation: Employers cannot know in advance whether a candidate will pass COMPASS
hesitations.why: COMPASS needs 40 points. C1 compares the offered salary with local PMET pay for the sector and age: 0 points below the 65th percentile, 10 from the 65th to below the 90th, and 20 at the 90th or above. C2 scores qualifications: 10 for degree-equivalent, 20 for MOM's top-tier list, and qualifications need verification proof (required since 1 Sep 2023). C3 and C4 depend on the firm's own nationality mix and local PMET share, so the same candidate can score differently at different employers. The C5 shortage-occupation bonus (+20) can offset a low C1 score. Benchmark tables are refreshed periodically; which table applies to applications from 1 Jan 2027 was not re-verified, so use MOM's Self-Assessment Tool.

hesitations.hesitation: Seniority gap: many Singapore agentic-AI roles ask for 5 to 10+ years
hesitations.why: Verified 18 Oct 2026: Temasek's Full Stack Agentic AI Engineer role asks for 5–8 years, with at least 2 in AI/ML. Atlassian's Principal MLE asks for 6+. The DBS GenAI platform Tech Lead asks for a minimum of 10 years, including 3 in banking or financial services, plus an active Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect certification. Roles that fit about 2 years better: ByteDance asks for 2+ years as an ML engineer, and DBS's AVP AI Engineer asks for hands-on production experience with no stated minimum. A GovTech/NEA AI-enabled products role was previously reported at 3+ years (not re-verified). With 2+ years, Swaroop's evidence has to show production contribution to compensate.

hiring_routes.fits_when: A Singapore-registered employer hires for a full-time role paying at least the EP qualifying salary for the candidate's age, and the application passes COMPASS or is exempt. hiring_routes.key_requirements: The employer or an appointed agent applies, not the candidate. An overseas company without a Singapore office applies through a Singapore-based sponsor. Stage 1, qualifying salary (current): S$5,600 a month (financial services S$6,200), rising with age to S$10,700 (S$11,800) at 45+. This has applied to new applications since 1 Jan 2025 and to renewals since 1 Jan 2026. corrected.timezone:
Singapore (SGT) is UTC+8 and India (IST) is UTC+5:30. Neither observes daylight saving, so Singapore is always 2 h 30 min ahead of Bengaluru (https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/converted.html?p1=236&p2=438).
- A 09:00–18:00 SGT day is 06:30–15:30 IST.
- A 09:00–18:00 IST day is 11:30–20:30 SGT.
- With no one shifting hours, the shared window is 11:30–18:00 SGT (09:00–15:30 IST), 6.5 hours.
- The only friction is Singapore early-morning stand-ups (09:00 SGT = 06:30 IST).

Heuristic: among non-Singapore candidates, IST is one of the smaller offsets a Singapore team will meet, so time zone is a mild plus for remote, hybrid or pre-relocation periods and does not matter once he has relocated. The hours Swaroop will commit to, and whether he will relocate, are UNKNOWN. Show the fixed offset as fact and the availability window only as a placeholder ('[Core availability: HH:MM–HH:MM SGT]') until he confirms.
corrected.resume_norms:
Singapore norms as of Oct 2026. Most are practitioner heuristics from career guides; those guides, and the TAFEP page, could not be re-fetched on 18 Oct 2026.

- **Length:** 1–2 pages. Guides say two pages is widely accepted (unlike the US one-page norm), and some advise one page for early-career candidates. The site already offers a one-page and a detailed resume PDF, which covers both.
- **Header:** name, Bengaluru, email, LinkedIn, GitHub, site. Guides advise stating work-pass or residency status in the header because employers plan around passes and COMPASS. Use a placeholder only ('[Work authorization: ...]', '[Notice period: ...]') until Swaroop confirms. Never publish phone number or salary expectations; expect the recruiter to ask about notice period and expected salary at the first screen.
- **Omit photo, date of birth, age, marital status, NRIC/passport number:** TAFEP's fair-employment guidance discourages employers from collecting such fields at application stage (https://www.tal.sg/tafep/employment-practices/recruitment/preparing-job-application-forms; not re-fetched this pass).
- **ATS formatting:** single column, standard headings, no tables or text boxes, keywords mirrored from the job description, PDF.
- **Impact lines:** quantified and honestly scoped, e.g. 'Contributed to an enterprise agent platform at ResMed: 150+ AI assistants created; end-user chatbot deployment time weeks → minutes'.
- **Status labels:** keep labels such as 'active design' and 'prototype' on the resume too.
- **Education:** list M.Eng. AI & ML (Manipal School of Information Sciences, MAHE, 2026, CGPA 9.08) and B.E. (Sapthagiri College of Engineering, 2023). Keep certificates and transcripts ready: MOM has required verification proof for qualifications in EP applications since 1 Sep 2023 (https://www.mom.gov.sg/-/media/mom/documents/work-passes-and-permits/compass/list-of-verification-portals.pdf).
- **Research:** list as 'in progress, not peer-reviewed; pre-registered'.

Sources: https://sg.jobstreet.com/career-advice/article/resume-format ; https://visualcv.com/international/singapore-resume ; https://www.roberthalf.com/sg/en/insights/landing-job/resume

corrected.resume_norms:
Heuristics ([U], not re-checked; check country guidance before use):
- US and Canada: 1 to 2 pages; no photo, date of birth, marital status or nationality, because employers avoid them under anti-discrimination law (https://www.eeoc.gov/prohibited-employment-policiespractices).
- UK and Ireland: a 'CV' of about 2 pages, no photo or date of birth (Equality Act 2010 context: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/equality-act-2010-guidance).
- Germany, Austria, Switzerland: a tabular reverse-chronological Lebenslauf; a photo is traditional but optional and increasingly left out in tech; English CVs are widely accepted at international tech employers.
- Netherlands and Nordics: concise, no photo needed.
- Japan: Japanese companies may ask for a rirekisho plus shokumu keirekisho; foreign-affiliated and tech firms usually accept an English CV.
- Singapore and Australia: about 2 to 3 pages, no photo; Singapore's fair-employment guidelines discourage age-related details (https://www.tal.sg/tafep).
- Gulf: photo and nationality are still common but optional.

1. THE '6 SECONDS' CLAIM. [S] TheLadders 2012: about 30 recruiters over 10 weeks; initial fit/no-fit about 6 s; about 80% of time on name, current title/company, current dates, previous title/company, previous dates and education; otherwise keyword scanning. [S] 2018 rerun: 7.4 s; simple layouts with clear headings did best. Limits: small samples, vendor study, not peer-reviewed, triage not hiring, generalist recruiters. A '11.2 seconds' figure attributed to ResumeGenius (2025) is unverified; do not cite it. Practical reading: put the six data points plus one proof number where the eye lands first, and let depth sit one click away.

2. HOW AI SOURCING TOOLS AND LLM ASSISTANTS FIND CANDIDATES ([U]). LinkedIn Recruiter's AI-assisted search and Hiring Assistant (announced Oct 2024) work from LinkedIn profile text and Open to Work preferences, so LinkedIn headline, About, Experience and Skills wording matter more than the personal site for LinkedIn sourcing. Third-party sourcing platforms aggregate public profiles (LinkedIn, GitHub, personal sites, papers). ChatGPT search, Perplexity and Claude fetch pages through their own crawlers and user-triggered fetchers (OpenAI: OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, GPTBot; Perplexity: PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User; Anthropic: ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot). Vercel/MERJ (Dec 2024) found the crawlers it measured from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, ByteDance and Perplexity did not render JavaScript; Gemini (via Googlebot) and Applebot do. Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode need only normal indexing plus snippet eligibility. Implication: every case study needs its own static URL whose raw HTML contains the content, a descriptive title and an H1, and the six data points in plain text.

3. /llms.txt. [U] Proposed by Jeremy Howard on 3 Sep 2024 (spec at llmstxt.org): a Markdown file with a required H1, optional blockquote summary and H2 link lists. A community proposal with no standards-body backing. [U] Google representatives said in 2025 that Google does not use it; [S] Google's AI optimization guide (changelog 15 Jun 2026) reportedly says such files are not needed and are ignored by Google Search. No statement from OpenAI, Anthropic or Perplexity that they read it for search or citation was found. Recommendation: optional, low cost, no expected benefit. If added, keep it to about 20 lines listing the static case-study URLs; never a substitute for crawlable HTML. With .nojekyll present [L], it would be served as-is from the repo root.

4. STRUCTURED DATA ([U]). schema.org ProfilePage (mainEntity Person); Person supports name, jobTitle, worksFor, alumniOf, knowsAbout, homeLocation, image, url, sameAs; SoftwareSourceCode supports codeRepository, programmingLanguage, author, license. Google's ProfilePage documentation (Nov 2023) requires mainEntity with a name and recommends sameAs, image, description and dates; a portfolio is not guaranteed any visual rich result, so treat it as entity clarity. Google has no rich result for SoftwareSourceCode. Markup must describe visible content. Recommended for home and about: ProfilePage with mainEntity Person (@id site#person, name 'Swaroop Chand J C', jobTitle, worksFor ResMed, alumniOf MAHE and Sapthagiri College of Engineering, homeLocation Bengaluru, knowsAbout from the stack list, sameAs LinkedIn and GitHub; email only if he wants it). Never include nationality, authorization or phone. Research page: SoftwareSourceCode with codeRepository https://github.com/swaroopchandrashekar13/reasearch, programmingLanguage Python, author @id site#person, description saying 'in progress, not peer-reviewed'. Add <link rel=canonical> on every page ([L] none today).

5. WHY THE HASH-ROUTED SITE IS WEAK FOR CRAWLERS. [L] Deep content lives in 26 <template> elements (13 case studies) swapped in by a hashchange router; links point to ./work/<slug>/index.html, which does not exist on main. Consequences: (a) [U] Google drops the fragment, so the 13 case studies cannot rank or be cited individually; (b) template contents are inert per the HTML spec, so Googlebot's rendered page likely shows only the home copy (confirm with Search Console URL Inspection); (c) non-JS crawlers following the real-path links get GitHub Pages 404s; (d) every view shares one title and description in the raw HTML. Fix: extend tools/split.py to emit a full static page (shell plus page fragment, its own title, meta description, canonical and JSON-LD) at each path the links already use. Keep the router only as progressive enhancement, or drop it. Run tools/qa.mjs against the static paths.
